<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">PART I</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a id="_Toc347923513" name="_Toc347923513"><!--Anchor--></a><a id="_Toc347923617" name="_Toc347923617"><!--Anchor--></a><a id="_Toc381523557" name="_Toc381523557"><!--Anchor--></a><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><u><a name="Item1.Business"><!--Anchor--></a>Item 1. Business</u></font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Heritage Financial Group, Inc. (&#8220;Heritage&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;), is a $1.4 billion holding company headquartered in Albany, Georgia.&#160; Heritage primarily conducts commercial banking, retail banking, mortgage banking and wealth management activities through its wholly owned subsidiary, HeritageBank of the South (&#8220;HeritageBank&#8221; or the &#8220;Bank&#8221;).&#160; As of December 31, 2013, HeritageBank operated in Georgia, Florida and Alabama through 27 full-service branch locations, 14 mortgage offices and 4 investment offices.<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>HeritageBank provides credit based products, deposit accounts, corporate cash management, investment support and other services to commercial and retail clients.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company was formed by its federally chartered predecessor, Heritage Financial Group (the &#8220;Predecessor&#8221;) in connection with a second-step conversion and public offering conducted in the latter half of 2010, in which the Predecessor merged into the Company and converted from a mutual holding company structure to a stock holding company structure (&#8220;Conversion&#8221;). In that merger, each public share of common stock of the Predecessor was exchanged for 0.8377 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock. The words &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our&#8221; and &#8220;us&#8221; in this Form 10-K refer to Heritage and HeritageBank on a consolidated basis.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, we had total assets of $1.4 billion, loans of $799.0 million, deposits of $1.1 billion and stockholders&#8217; equity of $125.1 million. Our executive offices are located at 721 N. Westover Boulevard, Albany, Georgia 31707. Our common stock is traded on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol &#8220;HBOS.&#8221; For more information about our business, see Item 7 - Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations &#8211; General.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Strategy.&#160; </font>Our business strategy is to operate a well-capitalized and profitable financial institution dedicated to serving the needs of our customers.&#160; We offer a broad range of products and services while stressing personalized and efficient customer service and convenient access to these products and services.&#160; We intend to continue to operate as a commercial and consumer lender.&#160; We have structured operations around a branch system that is staffed with knowledgeable and well-trained employees.&#160; Subject to capital requirements and our ability to grow in a reasonable and prudent manner, we may open or acquire additional branches as opportunities arise.&#160; In addition to our branch system, we continue to expand electronic services for our customers.&#160; We attempt to differentiate ourselves from our competitors by providing a higher level of customer service.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Expansion Efforts.</font>&#160; A key element of our business strategy is increasing our presence and growing the &#8220;Heritage&#8221; brand in the markets we currently serve and expanding our operations beyond our original Southwest Georgia market by entering new markets in other parts of Georgia, Florida, Alabama and other adjacent communities that present attractive opportunities for expansion consistent with our capital availability.&#160; This expansion of our market beyond southwest Georgia began in 2006, when we commenced operating a branch in Ocala, Florida.&#160; We have pursued this expansion program through both prudent, disciplined internal growth and strategic acquisitions.&#160; We have also hired highly regarded and experienced lending officers and commercial bankers and expanded into new market areas that are contiguous to our existing market areas.&#160; These recent activities reflect our ability to take advantage of these expansion opportunities.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2011, we completed two FDIC-assisted whole-bank acquisitions near Savannah, Georgia and in Statesboro, Georgia with combined loans of $247.2 million and deposits of $342.3 million.&#160;&#160; In April 2012, we opened a commercial banking office in Macon, Georgia, and in June 2012, we completed the purchase of a single branch in Auburn, Alabama with $10.9 million in loans and $18.7 million in deposits.&#160; In August 2012, we hired a new management team to operate our mortgage division which has led to significant growth in our mortgage business, particularly in the Atlanta, Georgia market.&#160; In March 2013, we completed an FDIC-assisted whole-bank purchase of a bank based in LaGrange, Georgia with $98.0 million in loans and $211.6 million in deposits, which were primarily located in Alabama, and in November 2013, we opened a commercial and mortgage banking office in Columbus, Georgia.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">5</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" href="#TableofContents">Table of Contents</a></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Market Area</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We intend to continue to be a community-oriented financial institution offering a variety of financial services to meet the needs of the communities we serve.&#160; At December 31, 2013, we primarily served our markets in Georgia through offices in Albany, LaGrange, Macon, Savannah, Statesboro, and Valdosta, Florida through offices in Lake City and Ocala and Alabama through offices in Auburn-Opelika, Birmingham-Hoover, Talledega-Sylacauga, and Valley.&#160; We occasionally make loans beyond our market area to meet customer needs and to develop new business.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following table sets forth our deposit market share and information regarding the local economy by market area, including acquisitions, as of June 30, 2013, based on the most recent data available from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) and SNL Financial.&#160; SNL Financial is a provider of news, financial data and analysis on the banking business.&#160; Most of our market areas fall within Metropolitan Statistical Areas (&#8220;MSA&#8221;) and were selected based on the market area&#8217;s significance to our operations.&#160; The significance of a market area includes such factors as the number of branches, the level of loans and deposits, or the current or potential future contribution to overall net income of Heritage.&#160; As of December 2013, the national unemployment rate was 6.7%, and the rates in Georgia, Florida and Alabama were 7.2%, 5.9% and 5.7%, respectively.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We face strong competition in originating commercial, real estate and other loans and in attracting deposits.&#160; Competition in originating real estate loans comes primarily from other banks, credit unions and mortgage bankers.&#160; Other banks, credit unions and finance companies also provide vigorous competition in consumer and commercial lending. We attract deposits through our branch office system.&#160; Competition for those deposits is principally from other banks and credit unions located in the same community, as well as mutual funds and other alternative investments.&#160; We compete for these deposits by offering superior service and a variety of deposit accounts at competitive rates.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><a id="RANGE!A1:U13" name="RANGE!A1:U13"><!--Anchor--></a><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Lending authority</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.</font>&#160; The Board of Directors has established lending authorities for its officers.&#160;&#160; Based on individual experience, Market Presidents and Commercial Lenders have established lending authorities for relationships with exposure up to $500,000, and Consumer and Mortgage Lenders have lending authorities for relationships with exposure up to $200,000.&#160; The Mortgage Division Co-Presidents have lending authorities for relationships with exposure up to $417,000, and the Regional Managers and Regional Presidents may make and approve secured loans for relationships with exposure up to $1.0 million.&#160; Regional Credit Officers or the Chief Banking Officer may approve secured loans for relationships with exposure up to $3.0 million.&#160; The Chief Executive Officer or the Chief Credit Officer may approve loans for relationships up to $5.0 million.&#160; Relationships and exposures that exceed $5.0 million must be approved by the Board of Directors.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are subject to lending limits established under Georgia law for loans to one borrower and the borrower's related entities.&#160; See Item 1 - How We Are Regulated - HeritageBank of the South for more information.&#160; Based on our capital level at December 31, 2013, the maximum amount under Georgia law that we could loan to any one borrower and the borrower's related entities was $21.6 million for fully secured loans (including loans secured by real estate for which we have an independent appraisal) and $13.0 million for all other loans.&#160; Internally, we have set a limit of $8.0 million for all loans to any one borrower and the borrower&#8217;s related entities.&#160; This internal limit may be exceeded with the approval of the Board of Directors.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Major loan customers</font>.&#160; Our ten largest lending relationships, excluding FDIC-acquired loans, are with commercial borrowers with total lending exposure, including undrawn lines of credit, of $76.6 million at December 31, 2013.&#160; These relationships consist of $10.0 million to a peanut shelling business secured by accounts receivable and inventory located primarily in southwest Georgia; $8.2 million to a specialty chemical business and their related interests in southwest Georgia; $8.0 million to a timber business located primarily in southeast Georgia; $7.9 million to a commercial warehousing and asset inventory management business in north Georgia; $7.7 million&#160; to a nursing home secured by real estate located in southwest Georgia; $7.6 million for the permanent financing of a hotel in north central Florida; $7.3 million secured primarily by multifamily and residential rental real estate in central Georgia; $7.0 million secured primarily by multifamily and residential rental real estate in southeast Georgia; $6.9 million to a retail pharmacy business secured by inventory and real estate located primarily in southwest Georgia; and $5.9 million to a nursing home and assisted living secured by real estate located in central Georgia.&#160; As of the date of this filing, these major customer relationships were performing and rated as pass credits.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For further information on credit quality, see Item 1 - Asset Quality - Delinquent Loans and - Classified Assets and see Item 7. Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;Residential Real Estate Lending.</font>&#160; We originate loans secured by first mortgages on one- to four-family residences, including home equity lines of credit, in our market area and outside our market area for customers whose primary residences are within our lending area.&#160; The majority of these loans are originated by us and sold to other lenders.&#160; See Item 1 &#8211; Loan Originations, Purchases, Sales, Repayments and Servicing for more information.&#160; At December 31, 2013, we had $206.6 million, or 26.2% of gross loans, in residential real estate loans including home equity lines of credit, of which $151.9 million were fixed-rate loans and $54.7 million were adjustable rate loans.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our home equity lines of credit totaled $29.1 million and accounted for 3.6% of gross loans at December 31, 2013.&#160; These loans may be originated in amounts, together with the amount of the existing first mortgage, of up to 100% of the value of the property securing the loan.&#160; Home equity lines of credit generally have a 3-year to 15-year draw period and require the payment of 1.5% of the outstanding loan balance per month during the draw period, which may be reborrowed at any time during the draw period.&#160; We also offer a 3-year to 15-year home equity line of credit that requires interest-only payments for the first five years, then fully amortizing payments over the remaining 10 years of the loan.&#160; At December 31, 2013, unfunded commitments on home equity lines of credit totaled $26.3 million.&#160; Other consumer loan terms vary according to the type of collateral, length of contract and creditworthiness of the borrower.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We generally underwrite our one&#8209; to four-family owner-occupied loans based on the applicant's employment and credit history and the appraised value of the subject property.&#160; We typically lend up to 90% of the lesser of the appraised value or purchase price for one- to four-family residential loans.&#160; Properties securing our one- to four-family loans are appraised by independent fee appraisers approved by the Board of Directors.&#160; We require our borrowers to obtain title insurance, hazard insurance and, if necessary, flood insurance.&#160; We currently originate one- to four-family mortgage loans on either a fixed- or adjustable-rate basis, as consumer demand dictates.&#160; Our pricing strategy for mortgage loans includes setting interest rates that are competitive with other local financial institutions and consistent with our internal needs.&#160; Fixed-rate loans generally have a 15- to 30-year term.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Adjustable-rate mortgage, or ARM, loans are generally offered with annual repricing with a maximum annual rate change of 2% and maximum overall rate change of 6%.&#160; We use a variety of indices to reprice our ARM loans.&#160; Our ARM loans generally provide for specified minimum and maximum interest rates, with a lifetime cap and floor, and a periodic adjustment of the interest rate over the rate in effect on the date of origination.&#160; As a consequence of using caps, the interest rates on these loans may not be as rate sensitive as is our cost of funds.&#160; Our ARM loans are written using generally accepted underwriting guidelines.&#160; ARM loans generally pose different credit risks than fixed-rate loans, primarily because as interest rates rise, the borrower's payment rise, increasing the potential for default.&#160; We do not offer initial discounted rates or &#8220;teaser&#8221; rates on adjustable-rate mortgage loans.&#160; Our real estate loans contain a &#8220;due on sale&#8221; clause allowing us to declare the unpaid principal balance due and payable upon the sale of the collateral.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We generally underwrite our non-owner-occupied, one- to four-family loans primarily based on a 1.25 times debt service coverage, though we also consider the applicant's creditworthiness and the appraised value of the property.&#160; We typically lend up to 85% of the lesser of the appraised value or purchase price for the residence.&#160; These loans are offered with a fixed rate or an adjustable rate typically using <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Wall Street Journal</font> prime rate as the index.&#160; These loans have terms of up to 15 years and are not assumable.&#160; We generally obtain title opinions from our counsel regarding these properties.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commercial Real Estate Lending</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.</font>&#160; We offer a variety of multifamily, nonresidential, and farmland real estate loans.&#160; These loans are secured primarily by multifamily dwellings, retail establishments, hotels, motels, warehouses, small office buildings, farmland, and other properties located in our market areas.&#160; At December 31, 2013, commercial real estate totaled $302.6 million, or 37.9% of gross loans. Nonresidential real estate totaled $256.6 million, or 32.1% of gross loans, and multifamily real estate totaled $22.7 million, or 2.9% of gross loans as December 31, 2013.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">11</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" href="#TableofContents">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Nonresidential and multifamily loans are originated with either a fixed or adjustable interest rate over various terms and structures.&#160; The interest rate on adjustable-rate loans is based on a variety of indices, generally determined through negotiation with the borrower.&#160; Loan-to-value ratios on our nonresidential and multifamily real estate loans typically do not exceed 80% of the appraised value of the property securing the loan.&#160; Loans secured by nonresidential and multifamily real estate are underwritten based on the income producing potential of the property and the financial strength of the borrower.&#160; The net operating income, which is the income derived from the operation of the property less all operating expenses, must be sufficient to cover the payments related to the outstanding debt.&#160; We generally require personal guarantees of the borrowers and an assignment of rents or leases in order to be assured that the cash flow from the project will be used to repay the debt.&#160; Appraisals on properties securing nonresidential and multifamily real estate loans are performed by independent state certified or licensed fee appraisers approved by the board of directors, with a second independent appraisal review performed if the loan exceeds $500,000.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We generally do not maintain a tax or insurance escrow account for loans secured by nonresidential and multifamily real estate.&#160; In order to monitor the adequacy of cash flows on income-producing properties, the borrower is generally required to provide periodic financial information.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans secured by nonresidential and multifamily real estate properties generally involve a greater degree of credit risk than single family residential mortgage loans.&#160; These loans typically involve large balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers.&#160; Because payments on loans secured by nonresidential and multifamily real estate properties are often dependent on the successful operation or management of the properties, repayment of these loans may be subject to adverse conditions in the real estate market or the economy.&#160; If the cash flow from the project is reduced, or if leases are not obtained or renewed, the borrower's ability to repay the loan may be impaired.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our loans secured by farmland totaled $23.4 million, or 2.9% of gross loans, and are originated with either a fixed or adjustable interest rate over a three-or five-year term with a balloon payment generally based on a 15-year amortization.&#160; The interest rate on adjustable-rate loans is based on a variety of indices, generally determined through negotiation with the borrower.&#160; Loan-to-value ratios on our farmland loans typically do not exceed 80% of the appraised value of the property securing the loan.&#160; Farmland loans are underwritten based on the income-producing potential of the property and the financial strength of the borrower.&#160; In order to monitor the adequacy of cash flows from farm operations, the borrower is required to provide periodic financial information.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans secured by farmland generally involve a greater degree of credit risk than one- to four-family residential loans.&#160; These loans typically involve large balances, and repayments are often dependent on the successful operation of the farm, making them subject to adverse weather and economic conditions.&#160; If the cash flow from the farm operations declines, the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the loan is impaired.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Construction and Land Lending</font>.&#160; Our construction loan portfolio consists of loans for the construction of one- to four-family residences, multifamily residences and commercial properties.&#160; Construction lending generally affords us an opportunity to receive interest at rates higher than those obtainable from residential lending and to receive higher origination and other loan fees.&#160; In addition, construction loans are generally made with adjustable rates of interest for six- to nine-month terms, with interest-only payments due during the construction period.&#160; At December 31, 2013, we had $50.2 million in construction loans outstanding, representing 6.3% of gross loans.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Construction loans also involve additional risks because funds are advanced upon the security of the project under construction, which is of uncertain value prior to the completion of construction.&#160; Moreover, because of the uncertainties inherent in estimating construction costs, delays arising from labor problems, material shortages, and other unpredictable contingencies, it is relatively difficult to evaluate accurately the total loan funds required to complete a project, and the related loan&#8209;to&#8209;value ratios.&#160; We fund our construction loans based on percentage of completion as determined by physical property inspections.&#160; Acquisition and development loans are required to be paid down as lots are sold, though on an accelerated basis so that we are repaid before all the lots are sold.&#160; See Item 1 &#8211; Asset Quality &#8211; Classified Assets for additional information.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commercial and Industrial Lending</font>.&#160; At December 31, 2013, commercial business loans totaled $101.2 million or 12.7% of gross loans.&#160; Our commercial business lending activities encompass loans with a variety of purposes and security, including loans to finance accounts receivable, agricultural production, inventory and equipment.&#160; Our commercial business lending policy includes credit file documentation and analysis of the borrower's background, capacity to repay the loan, the adequacy of the borrower's capital and collateral as well as an evaluation of other conditions affecting the borrower.&#160; Analysis of the borrower's past, present and future cash flows is also an important aspect of our credit analysis.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">12</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" href="#TableofContents">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Commercial business loans are generally secured by business assets, such as accounts receivable, equipment and inventory.&#160; This collateral may depreciate over time, may be difficult to appraise and may fluctuate in value based on the success of the business.&#160; As a result, the availability of funds for the repayment of commercial business loans may be substantially dependent on the success of the business itself (which, in turn, is often dependent in part upon general economic conditions).&#160; We generally obtain personal guarantees on our commercial business loans.&#160; Nonetheless, these loans are believed to carry higher credit risk than traditional single family loans.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Consumer and Other Lending</font>.&#160; We offer a variety of secured consumer loans, new and used auto loans, boat and recreational vehicle loans, and loans secured by deposit accounts. We also offer low dollar, unsecured loans and consumer credit cards.&#160; We originate our consumer and other loans primarily in our market areas.&#160; At December 31, 2013, our consumer and other loan portfolio totaled $24.0 million, or 3.0% of gross loans.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We originate auto loans on a direct basis, and auto loans may be written for up to six years and usually have fixed rates of interest.&#160; Loan-to-value ratios are up to 100% of the sales price for new autos and 100% of retail value on used autos, based on valuation from official used car guides.&#160; Consumer loans generally have shorter terms to maturity, which reduces our exposure to changes in interest rates, and carry higher rates of interest than do one- to four-family residential mortgage loans.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management believes that offering consumer loan products helps to expand and create stronger ties to our existing customer base by increasing the number of customer relationships and providing cross-market selling opportunities.&#160; Consumer loans may entail greater risk than do single family residential mortgage loans, particularly in the case of consumer loans that are secured by rapidly depreciable assets, such as automobiles and recreational vehicles.&#160; In these cases, any repossessed collateral for a defaulted loan may not provide an adequate source of repayment of the outstanding loan balance.&#160; As a result, consumer loan collections are dependent on the borrower's continuing financial stability and, thus, are more likely to be adversely affected by job loss, divorce, illness, or personal bankruptcy.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a id="_Toc381523562" name="_Toc381523562"><!--Anchor--></a>Loan Originations, Purchases, Sales, Repayments and Servicing</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We originate one- to four-family residential mortgage loans primarily through referrals from real estate agents, builders and from existing customers.&#160; Loan origination fees earned totaled $1.4 million, $1.3 million and $814,000 for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While we originate both adjustable-rate and fixed-rate loans, our ability to originate loans is dependent upon customer demand for loans in our market areas.&#160; Demand is affected by competition and the interest rate environment.&#160; In periods of economic uncertainty, the ability of financial institutions, including ours, to originate or purchase large dollar volumes of real estate loans may be substantially reduced or restricted, which in turn would lower our interest income.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to the categories of loans originated by us and described above, as of December 31, 2013, $114.2 million, or 14.3% of gross loans, consisted of loans acquired through FDIC-assisted acquisitions, with $50.9 million covered under loss-sharing agreements with the FDIC. Due diligence performed on these loans was limited due to the quick timing required for these transactions; however, the loss-sharing agreements with the FDIC provides coverage for 80% of the covered loan balance, which significantly mitigates the credit risk exposure for these loans.&#160; See Item 8 - Note 6 of the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information about these loans acquired through FDIC-assisted acquisitions.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have agreements with mortgage lenders, pursuant to which we originate and fund residential mortgage loans for these lenders in accordance with their policies, terms, and conditions.&#160; We typically charge the borrower an origination fee for processing the application in accordance with the lender's specifications.&#160; We also may earn a premium on these loans based on the difference between carrying value of the loan and the value purchased by a third party.&#160; During 2013, we originated $407.4 million of mortgage loans held for sale, generating approximately $12.0 million in mortgage banking income on these loans compared to <a id="OLE_LINK3" name="OLE_LINK3"><!--Anchor--></a><a id="OLE_LINK4" name="OLE_LINK4"><!--Anchor--></a>$137.4 million originated for 2012 generating approximately $5.7 million in mortgage banking income on those loans.&#160; We also sold $20.8 million of mortgage loans to the U.S. government sponsored agencies (&#8220;GSEs&#8221;) during 2013, and, separately, recorded a gain of $202,000 related to the mortgage servicing rights for those loans.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">13</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" href="#TableofContents">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to interest earned on loans and loan origination fees, we receive fees for loan commitments, late payments and other miscellaneous services.&#160; The fees vary from time to time, generally depending on the supply of funds and other competitive conditions in the market.&#160; Fees for late payments totaled $201,000, $214,000 and $246,000 for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a id="_Toc381523563" name="_Toc381523563"><!--Anchor--></a>Asset Quality</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">When a borrower fails to make a required payment on a loan, we attempt to cure the delinquency by contacting the borrower.&#160; Delinquent consumer loan customers are contacted by the lender and a centralized collections department.&#160; Delinquent commercial loan customers are contacted by the lender and are turned over to our special assets division if collection efforts by the lender are not successful.&#160; If the borrower does not cure the delinquency, we undertake an analysis of the best means to maximize our return through collection efforts, which may include litigation, taking a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, agreeing to a short sale, and/or initiating foreclosure proceedings.&#160; In the event we take title to underlying collateral, we generally seek to sell the asset as soon as practicable.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Delinquent Loans.</font>&#160; The table below sets forth the contractual principal balances by category of loans, excluding loans acquired through FDIC-assisted acquisitions, that were 30 to 89 days past due and still accruing interest at December 31, 2013.&#160; At all dates presented, we had no accruing loans 90 days or more delinquent.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the year ended December 31, 2013, approximately $462,000 of gross interest income would have been recorded had the non-accruing loans been current in accordance with their original terms.&#160; No significant amount was included in interest income on these loans for this period.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See Item 7 &#8211; Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations &#8211; Comparison of Financial Condition at December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012 - Delinquencies and Nonperforming Assets for more information on our non-performing assets.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Loans of Concern.</font>&#160; In addition to the nonperforming assets set forth in the table above, as of December 31, 2013, there was also an aggregate of $11.2 million of loans with respect to which known information about the possible credit problems of the borrowers have caused management to have doubts as to the ability of the borrowers to comply fully with present loan repayment terms and that may result in the future inclusion of those loans in the non&#8209;performing asset categories.&#160; <a id="OLE_LINK5" name="OLE_LINK5"><!--Anchor--></a><a id="OLE_LINK6" name="OLE_LINK6"><!--Anchor--></a>These loans include all criticized and classified loans and certain other past due loans that are not in a non-performing loan category.&#160; These loans have been considered in management's determination of the adequacy of our allowance for loan losses.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, we had three other loans of concern of over $1.0 million totaling approximately $5.2 million.&#160; The largest was a $2.2 million loan secured by the land used for a recreational vehicles park in Ocala, Florida.&#160; The remaining loans of concern at December 31, 2013 consisted of a $2.0 million loan secured by land in Ocala, Florida and a $1.0 million loan secured by residential properties in Albany, Georgia.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Classified Assets.</font>&#160; Federal regulations provide for the classification of loans and other assets, such as debt and equity securities considered to be of lesser quality, as substandard, doubtful or loss.&#160; An asset is considered substandard if it is inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if any.&#160; Substandard assets include those characterized by the distinct possibility that HeritageBank will sustain some loss if the deficiencies are not corrected.&#160; Assets classified as doubtful have all of the weaknesses inherent in those classified substandard, with the added characteristic that the weaknesses present make collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, highly questionable and improbable.&#160; Assets classified as loss are those considered uncollectible and of such little value that their continuance as active assets of HeritageBank are not warranted.&#160; See Item 8 - Note 5 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">When HeritageBank classifies problem assets as either substandard, doubtful, or loss, the loans are charged down to appraised value less selling costs while specific allowances are used for loans that do not qualify for a charge-off but the loss can be reasonably estimated.&#160; In addition, we establish general allowances based on historical loss history and migration analysis.&#160; General allowances represent loss allowances that have been established to recognize the inherent risk associated with lending activities, but which, unlike specific allowances, have not been allocated to particular problem assets.&#160; Our determination as to the classification of its assets and the amount of its valuation allowances is subject to review by the FDIC and the Georgia Department of Banking and Finance (&#8220;GDBF&#8221;), which may order the establishment of additional general or specific loss allowances.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We regularly review the problem assets in our portfolio to determine whether any assets require classification in accordance with applicable regulations.&#160; On the basis of management's review of our assets, at December 31, 2013, we had $19.6 million of our assets internally classified, of which $17.5 million consisted of loans and $2.1 million of other real estate and repossessions.&#160; All of these assets were classified as substandard.&#160; We had no assets classified as doubtful or loss at December 31, 2013.&#160; The total amount classified represented 15.7% of our equity capital and 1.4% of our assets at December 31, 2013.&#160; All of our $9.4 million in nonaccruing loans at December 31, 2013, were included in our classified assets at that date, and the <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">allowance for loan losses </font>related to those nonaccruing loans at that date was $1.5 million, or 15.8% of the nonaccruing loan balance.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">16</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-RIGHT-WIDTH: 0px; BACKGROUND-COLOR: #000000; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; BORDER-TOP-WIDTH: 0px; BORDER-BOTTOM-WIDTH: 0px; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both; BORDER-LEFT-WIDTH: 0px" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" href="#TableofContents">Table of Contents</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Allowance for Loan Losses</font>.&#160; We maintain an allowance for loan losses to absorb probable incurred losses in the loan portfolio.&#160; In evaluating the level of the allowance for loan losses, management considers the types of loans and the amount of loans in the loan portfolio, historical loss experience, migration analysis, probability of default, adverse situations that may affect the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay, estimated value of any underlying collateral, prevailing economic conditions, and past due status and trends.&#160; We analyze the historical migration of loans through each risk rating category and analyze the history of losses as it relates to the various loan types and collateral types in order to evaluate and estimate the volume, magnitude and direction these events. These risk factors and other factors are applied to our review of pass credit loan pools and other assets specially mentioned loan pools. These factors are applied to the substandard loan pool; however, in addition to reviewing the pool, a select group of individual loans are reviewed.&#160; The results of the individual review are factored in with the historical loss analysis and applied to the pool.&#160; Impaired loans are reviewed individually for specific amounts that are representative of identified credit exposures that are readily predictable by the current performance of the borrower and underlying collateral while impaired loans with balances less than $500,000 typically use a historical loss analysis.&#160; See Item 8 - Note 5 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information about our allowance methodology.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, our allowance for loan losses was $9.0 million, or 1.1% of the total loan portfolio,<font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>compared with a balance of $9.1 million, or 1.4% of total loans at December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160; Total criticized and classified loans decreased by $4.9 million during the period to $20.6 million at December 31, 2013 from $25.5 million at December 31, 2012.&#160; Nonaccrual loans decreased $5.2 million during the period to $9.4 million at December 31, 2013 compared with $14.7 million at December 31, 2012.&#160; The decrease in nonaccrual loans from 2012 was primarily driven by improving trends in our loan portfolio.&#160; Loans past due thirty days and still accruing decreased by $1.1 million to $1.0 million at December 31, 2013 compared with $2.1 million at December 31, 2012.&#160; See Item 8 - Note 5 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information about our loan portfolio.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 8pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">17</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" href="#TableofContents">Table of Contents</a></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance for loan losses is maintained at a level which management believes is adequate to absorb all probable losses on loans then present in the loan portfolio.&#160; The amount of the allowance is affected by:&#160; (1) loan charge&#8209;offs, which decrease the allowance; (2) recoveries on loans previously charged&#8209;off, which increase the allowance; (3) the provision for possible loan losses charged against income, which increases the allowance; and (4) credit mark transfers as a result of acquired loan pools experiencing credit losses in excess of the fair value discounts established, which increase the allowance.&#160; The allowance is discussed further in Item 8 - Notes 1 and 5 to the Consolidated Financial Statements and Item 7 - Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations - <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Critical Accounting Policies - </font>Allowance for Loan Losses.&#160; The following table sets forth an analysis of our allowance for loan losses.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Investment Activities</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Georgia savings banks have the authority to invest in various types of liquid assets, including United States Treasury obligations, securities of various federal, state and local agencies and jurisdictions, including callable agency securities, certain certificates of deposit of insured banks and savings institutions, certain bankers' acceptances, repurchase agreements, federal funds, and other investments.&#160; Subject to various restrictions, Georgia savings banks also may invest their assets in investment grade commercial paper and corporate debt securities and mutual funds whose assets conform to the investments that a Georgia savings bank is otherwise authorized to make directly.&#160; See "How We Are Regulated - HeritageBank of the South - Georgia Regulation" for a discussion of additional restrictions on our investment activities.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Chief Financial Officer and Chief Accounting Officer have the basic responsibility for the management of our investment portfolio. They consider various factors when making decisions, including the marketability, maturity, and tax consequences of the proposed investment.&#160; The maturity structure of investments will be affected by various market conditions, including the current and anticipated slope of the yield curve, the level of interest rates, the trend of new deposit inflows, and the anticipated demand for funds via deposit withdrawals and loan originations and purchases.&#160; The general objectives of our investment portfolio are to provide liquidity when loan demand is high, to assist in maintaining earnings when loan demand is low and to maximize earnings while satisfactorily managing risk, including credit risk, reinvestment risk, liquidity risk and interest rate risk.&#160; See Item 7 - Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations - Asset and Liability Management and Market Risk.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our investment securities currently consist of mortgage-backed securities, federal agency securities, preferred stocks, state and local government securities, and corporate debt securities.&#160;&#160; As a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank of Atlanta (&#8220;FHLB&#8221;), we hold $7.3 million of stock, the minimum amount of stock the FHLB allows based on our level of borrowings.&#160; See Item 8 - Note 4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements for more information about our investments.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following table sets forth the composition of our securities portfolio and other investments at the dates indicated.&#160; Our securities portfolio at December 31, 2013, did not contain securities of any single issuer with an aggregate book value in excess of 10% of our equity capital, excluding those issued by the United States Government or GSEs.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a id="_Toc381523565" name="_Toc381523565"><!--Anchor--></a>Sources of Funds</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.</font>&#160; Our sources of funds are deposits, borrowings, payment of principal and interest on loans, interest earned on or maturation of other investment securities and funds provided from operations.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Deposits.</font>&#160; We offer a variety of deposit accounts to both consumers and businesses having a wide range of interest rates and terms.&#160; Our deposits consist of savings and checking accounts, money market deposit accounts, NOW accounts, demand accounts, and certificates of deposit.&#160; We solicit deposits primarily in our market areas and rely on competitive pricing policies, marketing and customer service to attract and retain these deposits.&#160; In addition, we solicit brokered deposits when terms and rates are more favorable than those in the markets we serve.&#160; At December 31, 2013, we had $111.5 million in brokered deposits, of which $103.3 million were Certificate of Deposit Account Registry Service<font size="2"><sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">&#174;</sup> or CDARS<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">&#174;</sup> One Way Buy deposits, and $8.2 million were customer balances placed in the Reciprocal CDARS<sup style="vertical-align: text-top; line-height: 1; font-size: smaller;">&#174;</sup> product.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The flow of deposits is influenced significantly by general economic conditions, changes in prevailing interest rates and competition.&#160; The variety of deposit accounts we offer has allowed us to be competitive in obtaining funds and to respond with flexibility to changes in consumer demand.&#160; We try to manage the pricing of our deposits in keeping with our asset and liability management, liquidity and profitability objectives, subject to competitive factors.&#160; Based on our experience, we believe that our deposits are relatively stable sources of funds.&#160; Despite this stability, our ability to attract and maintain these deposits and the rates paid on them has been and will continue to be significantly affected by market conditions.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under regulations of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (&#8220;FRB&#8221;), we are required to maintain noninterest-bearing reserves at specified levels against our transaction accounts, primarily checking and NOW accounts.&#160; At December 31, 2013, we were in compliance with these federal requirements and, as a result, would have been deemed to be in compliance with a similar reserve requirement under Georgia law.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Borrowings</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.</font>&#160; Although deposits are our primary source of funds, we may utilize borrowings when they are a less costly source of funds, when we desire additional capacity to fund loan demand, or when they meet our asset/liability management goals.&#160; Our borrowings consist of advances from the FHLB, federal funds purchased, and securities sold under repurchase agreements.&#160; See Item 8 - Notes 19 and Note 20 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Advances from the FHLB require borrowing capacity supported by the pledging of certain loans or securities.&#160; These advances may be made pursuant to several different credit programs, each of which has its own interest rate, range of maturities, and call features.&#160; At December 31, 2013, we had $131.4 million in FHLB advances outstanding, including a $4.3 million fair value adjustment for advances acquired with the Frontier acquisition, and the ability to borrow an additional $25.2 million.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have the ability to borrow from securities broker-dealers and customers by pledging investments.&#160; These arrangements are known as securities sold under repurchase agreements.&#160; These borrowings can be done on an overnight, short-term or long-term basis.&#160; As of December 31, 2013, we had $30.0 million borrowed under long-term agreements with broker-dealers and $5.3 million borrowed under overnight agreements with customers.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We also have the ability to borrow up to $74.0 million from correspondent banks, pursuant to renewable lines of credit.&#160; In addition, we also borrow from Chattahoochee Bank of Georgia on an overnight basis, depending on their liquidity needs.&#160; At December 31, 2013, we had approximately $2.4 million in federal funds purchased from that bank compared with $417,000 at December 31, 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are authorized to borrow from the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's &#8220;discount window" after we have exhausted other reasonable alternative sources of funds, including FHLB advances.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a id="_Toc381523566" name="_Toc381523566"><!--Anchor--></a>Subsidiary and Other Activities</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are engaged in the sale of securities and insurance products to customers through an agreement with a third-party broker-dealer.&#160; During the years ended December 31, 2013 and 2012, we earned $2.1 million and $1.8 million, respectively, in gross fees and commissions from this activity.&#160; This activity is conducted in accordance with applicable provisions of federal and state insurance and securities laws.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2008, we acquired 4.9% of the outstanding shares of Chattahoochee Bank of Georgia, a de novo bank in Gainesville, Georgia, for approximately $1.0 million.&#160; This investment provides us with the opportunity to further expand in Northeast Georgia.&#160; We also participate in loans generated by Chattahoochee Bank of Georgia that exceed its legal lending limits, allowing us to generate loan volume and exposure to the northeast Georgia market without incurring building and personnel costs.&#160; O. Leonard Dorminey, our President and Chief Executive Officer, serves on the board of directors, executive committee and loan committee of Chattahoochee Bank of Georgia.&#160; As of December 31, 2013, we had $7.3 million in loan participations and $2.4 million in federal funds purchased from Chattahoochee Bank of Georgia.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other than HeritageBank, we currently do not have any active subsidiaries.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a id="_Toc381523567" name="_Toc381523567"><!--Anchor--></a>Employees</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013, we had a total of 426 full-time equivalent employees.&#160; Our employees are not represented by any collective bargaining group.&#160; Management considers its employee relations to be good.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a id="_Toc274674178" name="_Toc274674178"><!--Anchor--></a><a id="_Toc381523568" name="_Toc381523568"><!--Anchor--></a>How We Are Regulated</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Set forth below is a brief description of material information regarding certain laws and regulations that are and will be applicable to Heritage and HeritageBank.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Heritage is a savings and loan holding company subject to regulation and supervision by the FRB.&#160; The FRB requires that Heritage serve as a source of financial and managerial strength for HeritageBank, particularly when HeritageBank is in financial distress.&#160; HeritageBank is a Georgia savings bank subject to regulation and supervision by the GDBF and the FDIC, which also insures our deposits.&#160; The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the &#8220;Dodd-Frank Act&#8221;) created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (&#8220;CFPB&#8221;) that has authority to promulgate regulations intended to protect consumers with respect to financial products and services, including those provided by HeritageBank, and to restrict unfair, deceptive or abusive conduct by providers of consumer financial products and services.&#160; These regulations had previously been enacted by HeritageBank&#8217;s primary federal regulator.&#160; As a public company, Heritage is subject to the regulation and reporting requirements of the SEC.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 39.6pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Legislation is introduced from time to time in the United States Congress and Georgia General Assembly that may affect our operations.&#160; In addition, the regulations governing Heritage and HeritageBank may be amended from time to time by the GDBF, the FDIC, the FRB, the CFPB or the SEC, as appropriate.&#160; </font>Any legislative or regulatory changes, including those resulting from the Dodd-Frank Act, in the future could adversely affect our operations and financial condition.&#160; <font style="FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See &#8220;The Dodd-Frank Act&#8221; below for additional information on its provisions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; FONT-FAMILY: ''Times New Roman'', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The GDBF, the FDIC and the FRB, as appropriate, have extensive enforcement authority over Heritage and HeritageBank.&#160; This enforcement authority includes, among other things, the ability to assess civil money penalties, to issue cease-and-desist or removal orders and to initiate injunctive actions.&#160; In general, these enforcement actions may be initiated for violations of laws and regulations and unsafe or unsound practices.&#160; Other actions or inactions may provide the basis for enforcement action, including misleading or untimely reports filed with the FDIC.&#160; Except under certain circumstances, public disclosure of formal enforcement actions by the FDIC and FRB is required by law.</div>
